Headteacher's Welcome
Whether you are a parent, child, friend, neighbour or visitor, we want you to feel welcome and valued at Downs Infant School.
Our vision is to create a welcoming and inclusive school community where children can be happy and excited about their opportunities. We want to give children a voice and a feeling of worth. We nurture a culture of wanting to learn, and an ‘I can do it!’ attitude.

Admissions
Information for Parents/Carers
How do I apply for a place at Downs Infant School?
Brighton and Hove Council makes the arrangements for the admission of children to this school. Full information on arrangements for admission to schools in Brighton and Hove is contained in a booklet entitled ‘School Admissions in Brighton & Hove' available on-line at www.brighton-hove.gov.uk/schooladmissions.
A paper copy can be requested from:
The School Admissions Team Brighton and Hove City Council, King's House, Grand Avenue, Hove, East Sussex BN3 2LS
Tel: (01273) 293653 or e-mail schooladmissions@brighton-hove.gov.uk
The Local Authority do not use catchment areas for infant, junior or primary schools.
If the school is oversubscribed places are allocated to children in accordance with the following list of priorities:
1) Children in the care of a local authority or who were previously in care
2) Children with compelling medical or other exceptional reasons for attending the school (with supporting independent professional evidence).
(3) Sibling link - Children who in September of that year will have a brother or sister at the school or at a linked junior school (Downs Junior School in our case).
(4) Children transferring between a linked infant and junior school, subject to dates. This priority only applies at Junior transfer.
If it should be necessary to decide between children within any of these priority groups, this will be done by giving the places to those children who live closest to the school. There is no ‘catchment area’. The Local Authority applies specific software to determine home-to-school distance.

Wraparound Childcare (Rainbow Club)
Downs infants School offer wraparound childcare provision for children who attend Downs Infants school and operates on a term-time only basis.
The timings and cost for each session are detailed below:
7.45am – Start of the school day
End of the school day – 6.00pm
Rainbow Club wraparound care - All enquiries to: rainbowclub@downsinf.brighton-hove.sch.uk
Information for Parents/Carers

Reception
Learning
Reception
Children have the opportunity to 'freeflow' for much of the day between our four classrooms, the indoor activity area ('the ocean'), the outside covered area ('the beach') and the garden and we have been able to maintain much of this. We recognise that many children need to start from their own familiar experiences, and that creativity and problem-solving skills are important, so our role play areas are 'deconstructed' and 'basic' to allow all children to access the rich opportunities for language development and collaborative play available. Additional provocations are added to stimulate particular thinking, play or language at various times.

Knowledge Organisers
These documents highlight the key knowledge, concepts and vocabulary that we want children to learn in the units throughout the year. You might want to refer to these in helping your child at home.
